# package object

```go
import "github.com/otfabric/go-bacnet/server/object"
```

Package object is the object model served by package server: the Object interface, the Device object (clause 12.11) and the standard objects a supervisory client usually meets.

Objects are in-memory and safe for concurrent use. The server never holds a lock of its own while it calls an object. Applications may implement Object themselves; the built-in types embed Base.

This package does not import the server runtime, the client or the wire codecs below package service.

### type Calendar

```go
type Calendar struct {

}
```

### type EventConfig

```go
type EventConfig struct {
	NotificationClass uint32
	EventEnable       uint8  // EnableTo… bits
	NotifyType        uint32 // NotifyAlarm or NotifyEvent
	TimeDelay         uint32 // seconds a condition holds before it is reported
	// Analog.
	HighLimit, LowLimit, Deadband float32
	LimitEnable                   uint8 // LimitEnable… bits
	// Binary: the Present_Value that is off-normal (0 inactive, 1 active).
	AlarmValue uint32
	// Multi-state Input and Value: Alarm_Values, the Present_Values that
	// are off-normal (CHANGE_OF_STATE, clause 13.3.2), and Fault_Values,
	// the Present_Values that are a fault: Reliability is then
	// MULTI_STATE_FAULT (FAULT_STATE, clause 13.4.5). Each value is a state
	// 1..Number_Of_States.
	AlarmValues []uint32
	FaultValues []uint32
}
```

EventConfig enables intrinsic reporting on a point (clause 13.2): OUT\_OF\_RANGE for analog objects, CHANGE\_OF\_STATE for binary objects and for Multi-state Input and Value objects (clauses 12.18, 12.20), and FAULT for any object whose Reliability is not no-fault-detected.

### type File

```go
type File struct {
	*Base
	// contains filtered or unexported fields
}
```

File is an in-memory File object (clause 12.11). A start position of -1 in AtomicWriteFile appends. A write past the end of the file grows it as bacnet-stack's storage does (ports/posix/bacfile-posix.c): a stream file is extended with zero octets up to the start position, and records are appended after the last one, the actual start being returned. A read past the end is refused with invalid-file-start-position, the rule bacnet-stack applies to reads (h\_arf.c), and AtomicReadFile from the end returns no data with End\_Of\_File set.

### type FileAccessor

```go
type FileAccessor interface {
	StreamAccess() bool
	ReadStream(start int32, count uint32) (data []byte, eof bool, err error)
	WriteStream(start int32, data []byte) (actualStart int32, err error)
	ReadRecords(start int32, count uint32) (records [][]byte, eof bool, err error)

}
```

FileAccessor is implemented by File objects for AtomicReadFile and AtomicWriteFile (clauses 14.1, 14.2). Start positions and counts are in octets for stream access and in records for record access.

### type Notifier

```go
type Notifier func(Change)
```

Notifier receives changes; a Device installs one in every object it holds. Implementations of Object that report COV or events call it after a value changed, never while holding their own lock.

### type Object

```go
type Object interface {
	// Identifier returns the object identifier. It never changes.
	Identifier() bacnet.ObjectIdentifier
	// Name returns the current Object_Name.
	Name() string
	// ReadProperty returns a property value. An array property read without
	// an index returns the whole array as a constructed value; index 0 is the
	// array length. Errors are *bacnet.ErrorResponse values (see Err).
	ReadProperty(ctx context.Context, ref bacnet.PropertyReference) (bacnet.ApplicationValue, error)
	// WriteProperty writes a property. Errors are *bacnet.ErrorResponse
	// values (see Err).
	WriteProperty(ctx context.Context, w Write) error
	// Properties returns the identifiers of every property the object has, in
	// a stable order, and which of them are required by the standard for its
	// type (used for ReadPropertyMultiple ALL / REQUIRED / OPTIONAL).
	Properties() (all []bacnet.PropertyIdentifier, required map[bacnet.PropertyIdentifier]bool)
}
```

Object is one BACnet object served by a Device.

```go
type PointConfig struct {
	Instance    uint32
	Name        string
	Description string
	// Commandable gives a value object a priority array. Output objects are
	// always commandable, input objects never.
	Commandable bool

	// Analog.
	Units        uint32  // BACnetEngineeringUnits
	Value        float32 // initial Present_Value / Relinquish_Default
	COVIncrement float32 // default 0: every change notifies

	// Binary.
	Active       bool
	Polarity     uint32 // 0 normal, 1 reverse (inputs and outputs)
	ActiveText   string
	InactiveText string

	// Multi-state.
	NumberOfStates uint32 // required, >= 1
	State          uint32 // initial value, 1..NumberOfStates (default 1)
	StateText      []string

	// Events enables intrinsic reporting (analog and binary objects, and
	// Multi-state Input and Value objects).
	Events *EventConfig
}
```

### type Property

```go
type Property struct {
	// Value is the stored value. An array is a constructed value with one
	// element per array item.
	Value bacnet.ApplicationValue
	// Get, when set, computes the value on every read instead of Value. It
	// runs with the object's lock held for reading.
	Get func() bacnet.ApplicationValue
	// Set, when set, handles writes instead of the default (which stores a
	// value of one of Kinds). It runs with the object's lock held and returns
	// the properties whose value changed.
	Set func(w Write) ([]bacnet.PropertyIdentifier, error)
	// Writable makes the property writable through WriteProperty.
	Writable bool
	// Kinds are the value kinds a default write accepts.
	Kinds []bacnet.ValueKind
	// Array marks a BACnetARRAY (array index access, clause 12).
	Array bool
	// Required marks the property as required for the object type.
	Required bool
}
```

Property describes one property of a Base object.

### type Schedule

```go
type Schedule struct {
	*Base

	// datatype; ValueNull while undetermined

	// Present_Value is still to be written to the references

}
```

Schedule is a Schedule object (clause 12.24). Present\_Value is evaluated on every Poll against the server's clock: the highest-priority special event of Exception\_Schedule that is in effect and has a non-NULL value at the current time, otherwise the day's Weekly\_Schedule entry, otherwise Schedule\_Default; outside Effective\_Period it is Schedule\_Default. When Present\_Value changes it is written, at Priority\_For\_Writing, to every referenced property of an object of the same device.

#### func NewSchedule

```go
func NewSchedule(cfg ScheduleConfig) (*Schedule, error)
```

NewSchedule returns a Schedule object.

#### func (Schedule) Poll

```go
func (s *Schedule) Poll(ctx context.Context, now time.Time, dev *Device)
```

Poll implements Poller: Present\_Value is evaluated against the server's clock unless Out\_Of\_Service is TRUE, and a changed (or written) value is written to the references.

#### func (Schedule) PresentValue

```go
func (s *Schedule) PresentValue() bacnet.ApplicationValue
```

PresentValue returns Present\_Value.

#### func (Schedule) References

```go
func (s *Schedule) References() []DeviceObjectPropertyReference
```

References returns List\_Of\_Object\_Property\_References.

### type ScheduleConfig

```go
type ScheduleConfig struct {
	Instance    uint32
	Name        string
	Description string
	// EffectivePeriod limits the dates the schedule is in effect; nil means
	// always (both dates fully unspecified).
	EffectivePeriod *bacnet.DateRange
	// Weekly is Weekly_Schedule, Monday first.
	Weekly bacnet.WeeklySchedule
	// Exceptions is Exception_Schedule. A special event either has a
	// calendar entry or names a Calendar object (PeriodObject).
	Exceptions []bacnet.SpecialEvent
	// Default is Schedule_Default; its kind is the datatype of the schedule
	// (every time value is of that kind or NULL). A NULL default leaves the
	// datatype to the first non-NULL value of Weekly or Exceptions.
	Default bacnet.ApplicationValue
	// References is List_Of_Object_Property_References: the properties the
	// schedule writes Present_Value to.
	References []DeviceObjectPropertyReference
	// PriorityForWriting is 1..16 (default 16).
	PriorityForWriting uint8
	// MaxExceptions bounds Exception_Schedule (default 32) and MaxReferences
	// List_Of_Object_Property_References (default 32).
	MaxExceptions int
	MaxReferences int
}
```

ScheduleConfig configures a Schedule object.

### type StructuredView

```go

	*Base

	// nil when the property is absent

}
```

StructuredView is a Structured View object (clause 12.29). As in bacnet-stack's structured\_view.c, Node\_Type, Node\_Subtype, Subordinate\_List and Subordinate\_Annotations are writable. Writing the whole Subordinate\_List may change its length; Subordinate\_Annotations follows it (texts of removed entries are dropped, new entries get an empty text) and is written with as many texts as there are subordinates.


Log appends a record with the given time stamp when the log is enabled. The datum choice follows the value kind (REAL, BOOLEAN, ENUMERATED, Unsigned, INTEGER, BIT STRING, NULL).

```go

```

#### func (TrendLog) ReadProperty

```go

```

ReadProperty implements Object; Log\_Buffer is refused.

#### func (TrendLog) ReadRange

```go
func (tl *TrendLog) ReadRange(_ context.Context, prop bacnet.PropertyReference, q RangeQuery) (RangeResult, error)
```

ReadRange implements RangeReader for Log\_Buffer (clause 15.8). Where the standard leaves room the selection follows bacnet-stack (trendlog.c): by time with a positive count starts at the first record newer than the reference, with a negative count it ends at the last record older than it; by position and by sequence number clip the range to the buffer.

```go
	// Source records are only added with Log.
	Source         *bacnet.ObjectIdentifier
	SourceProperty bacnet.PropertyIdentifier
	LogInterval    time.Duration
	Enable         bool
}
```

### type WriteGuard

```go
type WriteGuard interface {
	BeforeWrite(ctx context.Context, obj bacnet.ObjectIdentifier, w Write) error
}
```

WriteGuard is an optional part of a Runtime. When the bound Runtime implements it, writes that objects of the Device make to other objects (a Schedule writing its List\_Of\_Object\_Property\_References) are checked with BeforeWrite first; a returned error leaves the property unchanged. The server implements it with its BeforeWrite hook.
